::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Scaling a matrix such that diagonal elements are $1$](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2184881/scaling-a-matrix-such-that-diagonal-elements-are-1), asked by [Mkty](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/414838/mkty) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-03-13; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> How can we scale a given matrix such that all the diagonal elements are equal to $1$. In particular what operations should be performed to obtain this kind of matrix.
>
> Suppose there is a matrix like 
>
> \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 3 & 1 & 4\\
> 3 & 2 & 2 & 4\\
> 1 & 2 & 7 & 7\\
> 4 & 4 & 7 & 7\end{pmatrix}
>
> I want to scale this matrix such that all diagonal elements are equal to $1$.
>
> Thanks in advance.
:::

Notice that when you multiply an $m \times n$ matrix $A$ on the left by a diagonal $m\times m$ matrix $D$, each row of $A$ is scaled by the corresponding nonzero entry in $D$.  Try it for $2\times2$ and $3\times3$ and you will see why.

Now you can work backwards: what $D$ will scale the rows of $A$ to make its diagonal terms equal to $1$?
